findings.summary: rails-run-a-workflow/SKILL.md's REFUTE stage still describes `stageOutputs` as carrying inline content, contradicting both the contract's own `refute-stage-output-input` Decision (paths only, 'never as content', 'each agent opens the file itself') and the actual refute.js interface, which takes `stageOutputPaths` and throws unless each value is a nonempty file-path string.
findings.evidence: `.agents/skills/rails-run-a-workflow/SKILL.md:162`: "`stageOutputs` carries the complete GROUND, DESIGN, and hidden-decision results: all three are required at L1..." -- this is the ONLY place the doc describes this input, and it names the wrong field and the wrong mechanism (content vs. path). Live code contradicts it: `.agents/workflows/refute.js:1242` `const stageOutputPaths = (input && input.stageOutputPaths) || {}`; `:1281` `throw new Error('refute: stageOutputPaths.${name} must be a nonempty file path')`; `:1357` the agent prompt reads "RECORDED RESULTS OF THE STAGES THAT RAN, as file paths — open and read each one yourself". `grep -n "opens the file\|open and read\|file path\|never as content" .agents/skills/rails-run-a-workflow/SKILL.md` returns zero matches -- the security-relevant, anti-forgery mechanism the contract decided on is entirely absent from the process doc. This is the exact gap refute-round-6's own Prove-It pass flagged for the code (refute-round-6-output.json, prove-it finding 1) and the round-6 hidden-decision-scan flagged as HIGH severity (hidden-decision-output-round6.json finding 1: 'refute.js validates only the SHAPE... and never re-reads the stage's own persisted run-record file'); the code was subsequently fixed to use `stageOutputPaths`, but the prose that a future orchestrator or agent would read to learn REFUTE's contract was never corrected to match, and even the locked contract's own Acceptance #23 still says 'under `stageOutputs`' (contract.md:653), so the internal inconsistency was carried all the way to the final, 'finished' state. A reader following the doc as written would supply inline content, get a runtime throw from the real code, and have to reverse-engineer the actual (safer) mechanism from source -- exactly the 'mismatch of existing records' and 'what would the human wrongly believe' failure Prove-It is required to hunt.
findings.fix: Rewrite `rails-run-a-workflow/SKILL.md`'s REFUTE Inputs line (and any other stage line naming `factsPath`/`ledgerPath`/`refutationPath` loosely) to state the actual mechanism: `refute.js` takes `stageOutputPaths` -- an object of file paths, never content -- and each adversary opens and reads the named file itself; L1 requires all three (`ground`, `design`, `hiddenDecisionScan`), L2 supplies only the stages that ran, L3 supplies none. Correct contract.md Acceptance #23 to name `stageOutputPaths` to match the Decision it is supposed to check, and rerun the full acceptance sweep after the edit.

findings.summary: The contract's own no-loss inventory still names `rails-read-me` as the destination for the 'Out-of-repo-root references' rule, but the rule actually lives in `rails-real-work` -- an undocumented, unapproved deviation from the locked contract text, and the destination the contract literally specifies is unreachable by every workflow script.
findings.evidence: `.dev/inprocess/2026-09-01-reorganize-rails/contract.md:547`: "`rails-run-a-workflow` — \"Out-of-repo-root references. Illegal — workers never add one, adversaries flag any found.\" | `rails-read-me`" -- this is the approved, locked destination. Live code disagrees: `grep -n "Out-of-repo-root" .agents/skills/*/SKILL.md` finds it only at `.agents/skills/rails-real-work/SKILL.md:66-69` ("### 11. Out-of-repo-root references"), and it is nowhere in `rails-read-me`. Separately, `grep -rn "rails-read-me" .agents/workflows/*.js` returns zero matches -- no workflow script loads `rails-read-me` at all, so had the rule actually landed at the contract's stated destination it would be unreachable by every worker and adversary, which is precisely the defect refute-round-6's Lie-catcher pass flagged (refute-round-6-output.json, lie-catcher finding 3: "A rule whose own text binds workers and adversaries was relocated to `rails-read-me`, the one rail no workflow prompt loads"). The actual placement in `rails-real-work` (loaded by `implement.js` per `.agents/workflows/implement.js:1339`) fixes the reachability problem, but nothing in `contract.md`, and no run-record file (`grep -rl "Out-of-repo-root" .dev/inprocess/2026-09-01-reorganize-rails/*.json .dev/inprocess/2026-09-01-reorganize-rails/*.md` finds it only in `implement-output.json`, `refute-round-6-output.json`, and `contract.md` itself -- never in a Decision or an approval quote), records this as an approved change to the locked no-loss inventory. Acceptance #1 requires 'every no-loss inventory row has one destination'; the row as written names a destination the delivered work does not use, so the acceptance criterion is not literally met, and the contract's Scope clause ('Scope changes ONLY by the human editing the contract...') was not satisfied for this specific relocation.
findings.fix: Edit contract.md's no-loss inventory row for the 'Out-of-repo-root references' rule to name `rails-real-work` as the destination (matching where the text actually now lives and where it is actually loaded), get Tim's explicit sign-off on that correction under the Scope rule, and re-verify Acceptance #1 against the corrected table.

AG0012  AG0013  AG0014  AG0016  AG0021  AG0028` header block. findings.summary: rule-phase.js does not carry the verbatim approved analyzer-ID instruction; it substitutes an unapproved band scheme that re-introduces the hardcoded analyzer range acceptance 19 forbids.
findings.evidence: Contract Decision `current-analyzer-id-source` (contract.md:143-147) says: "Replace the stale hardcoded analyzer range and ID examples with: > \"Follow the current analyzer implementations. Before choosing a `DiagnosticId`, read both `AnalyzerReleases.Shipped.md` and `AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md` and use the next free, never-used ID. Register the new ID in `AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md`.\"" The live text at `.agents/workflows/rule-phase.js:1291` instead reads: "... read every section of both `AnalyzerReleases.Shipped.md` and `AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md`, including `### Removed Rules`. IDs run in bands: AG00xx for architecture rules, AG01xx for native-interop rules, AGSxxxx for the security band. Take the highest ID ever used inside that band and add one. A retired ID counts as used ... Never fill a gap in the numbering." Acceptance 19 (contract.md:649) requires rule-phase.js to "contain no hardcoded stale analyzer range or next-ID example" — "AG00xx / AG01xx / AGSxxxx" is a hardcoded analyzer range. The substituted policy is option 2 of `hidden-decision-output-round6.json` finding #3 ("Change the instruction from 'the next free, never-used ID' to 'one above the highest ID ever assigned'"), which the scan surfaced as an unresolved forced choice for Tim; `grep -n -i "band|highest ID|fill a gap|Removed Rules" .dev/inprocess/2026-09-01-reorganize-rails/contract.md` returns nothing, so no Decision and no Tim words exist for it. The instruction also tells readers to consult `### Removed Rules`, a section the same run's own analyzer-file comment says cannot exist yet ("They cannot be listed under '### Removed Rules' because that section requires a prior shipped release"). Success definition requires ALL criteria met; acceptance 19 is unmet.

findings.summary: Three normative Communication rules were deleted with no owner anywhere in the nine rails, breaking the no-loss requirement in the success definition.
findings.evidence: `git show HEAD:.agents/skills/rails-read-me/SKILL.md` Communication section contains six bullets. Contract inventory row (contract.md:528) sends the complete unit to `rails-real-work`, and contract.md:515 states "The destination applies to the complete current source unit, including every `must`, `never`, `only`, `stop`, Practice, Violation, and Fix inside the named unit." Only three survive: direct-confirmation → rails-real-work #9, DECIDED-first → rails-real-work #10, self-contained reports → rails-run-a-workflow REPORT. The other three are gone from every rail. Verified by grep across all nine `SKILL.md` files: "literal question" NONE, "coined jargon" NONE, "expert audience" NONE, "concrete values" NONE, "verdict/answer" NONE, "preamble" NONE. The lost rules are "Open every message with the verdict/answer, not narration, preamble, or self-commentary", "Answer the literal question in the asker's vocabulary ... If the honest answer is 'it doesn't exist' or 'I didn't do it,' say that plainly and first", and "Plain, existing vocabulary — no coined jargon. State concrete values ... Assume an expert audience; don't explain basic concepts unasked." Contract success definition (contract.md:468) requires "every original normative rule has one recorded destination".

findings.summary: rails-read-me routes the shared communication standard to `how-to-communicate`, a skill this repository does not ship — acceptance 14 is unmet, and it re-creates the exact defect the immediately preceding commit fixed.
findings.evidence: `.agents/skills/rails-read-me/SKILL.md:32`: "- `how-to-communicate` owns the shared communication standard." `ls .agents/skills/` returns only the nine rails; `find . -iname "*how-to-communicate*"` returns nothing in the repository (`.claude/skills` is a symlink to `../.agents/skills`). Acceptance 14 (contract.md:644): "Each reference from the nine rails and every workflow script named in Surfaces resolves to an existing repository file or an approved memory-store description." My own reference sweep across all nine rails and all nine workflow scripts found `how-to-communicate` as the one reference that resolves to neither. The immediately preceding commit b504dc4 — "rails: stop the REPORT stage citing skills the repo does not ship" — removed this exact reference for this exact reason: "Neither is in this repo. Both exist only in Tim's home directory (~/.claude/skills and ~/.codex/skills), so a clone or a fresh agent reads a mandatory instruction pointing at files that are not there." The acceptance-14 proof recorded in `implement-output.json:116` is a hand-curated hardcoded list of 33 paths that omits `how-to-communicate` entirely — a check special-cased to pass rather than a scan of the actual references. Contract.md:627 required the agent to "Stop and present any rule with no destination or any conflict not settled by Decisions"; the conflict between inventory row 528 and acceptance 14 was implemented silently instead.

findings.evidence: Contract inventory row (contract.md:547): "| `rails-run-a-workflow` — \"Out-of-repo-root references. Illegal — workers never add one, adversaries flag any found.\" | `rails-read-me` |". Live location: `.agents/skills/rails-real-work/SKILL.md:66-69`, rail "### 11. Out-of-repo-root references". `rg -n -i 'out-of-repo-root|outside the repository root' .agents/skills/*/SKILL.md` returns hits only in rails-real-work; `rg -n -i 'repository root|repo root' .agents/skills/rails-read-me/SKILL.md` returns nothing (exit 1). `single-owner-map` (contract.md:11,18) assigns rails-read-me "Repository facts, locations, build commands, protected areas, shipping rules, and skill routing" and rails-real-work "Completeness, shortcuts, hacks, stale evidence, and report quality" — a repository-location rule is not rails-real-work's responsibility, so acceptance 1 ("Each of the nine skills contains only the responsibility assigned in `single-owner-map`") is unmet.
